This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Take Five vamp**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

For 5/4, grouped 3 + 2: a held chord on 1, a short one on the and of 2, then short chords on 4 and 5.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-pad.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="118" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-meter="5/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Charleston

A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-charleston.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="118" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-meter="5/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Take Five vamp, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** 5/4 grouped 3+2: held chord on 1, short on the and of 2, short chords on 4 and 5. It is the Charleston with two more beats.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="118" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-meter="5/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Take Five vamp","opts":{"compRhythm":"takefive"}},{"label":"Charleston (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 168 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="168" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-meter="5/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Take Five vamp","opts":{"compRhythm":"takefive"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Ebm7|Bbm7|Ebm7|Bbm7" data-tempo="168" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-meter="5/4" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Take Five vamp","opts":{"compRhythm":"takefive"}}]'></div>
